claims.statement: Treat Ghosts as a movement faction with weaker midgame development but unusually strong late-game closing options.
claims.conditions: The guide’s comparison is specifically to Cabal; the advantage depends on surviving the middle rounds and building enough plastic.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 326, published 2023-11-22; ruleset compatibility not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: Evaluative comparison by the hosts, not a measured faction ranking.

claims.statement: Use Quantum Entanglement to treat alpha and beta wormhole systems as mutually adjacent, while remembering that this ability does not include gamma or delta wormholes.
claims.conditions: This is the hosts’ reading of the faction ability; they flag expansion-specific exceptions and an unresolved edge case about Aetherstream.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 326 (2023-11-22); ruleset and later errata compatibility not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: The podcast recounts a designer response that was expressly uncertain about Aetherstream; do not generalize that ruling beyond its described case.

claims.statement: Exploit Slipstream’s extra movement from home or alpha/beta wormhole systems, but do not count on it from the Creuss Gate or gamma wormholes.
claims.conditions: The guide treats this restriction as strategically important; moving the flagship’s delta system does not make it a Slipstream start point.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 326 (2023-11-22); exact current wording not independently checked.
claims.uncertainty: The speakers criticize the restrictions, but their strategic recommendation assumes the printed ability as they describe it.

claims.statement: Compensate for the narrow starting fleet by prioritizing production and reinforcing the systems you can reach through the wormhole network.
claims.conditions: Ghosts begin with one carrier, two destroyers, two fighters and a space dock; spreading out without support can leave forces stranded.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 326 (2023-11-22); starting-unit description and strategic claims are not current-rules verified.
claims.uncertainty: Build priorities depend on slice resources, command-counter preference and table aggression.

claims.statement: Consider an early Malice take using the agent: the hosts describe sending the starting carrier there, flipping Malice for two trade goods, and gaining access to an extra early income source.
claims.conditions: This is a common opening option, not an obligation; sometimes waiting or choosing other reachable systems is better, and the extra trade good needed for another carrier still matters.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 326 (2023-11-22); agent timing, Malice values and costs not independently checked.
claims.uncertainty: The ASR varies proper nouns; the component reference confirms Emissary Taivra and Malice-related source discussion but does not make this rules verification.

claims.statement: In round one, look for a third dollar or trade good beyond home and Malice if you want to afford a second carrier while also taking Sling Relay.
claims.conditions: Industrial or hazardous planets, favorable Trade timing, or a neighbor’s exchange can close the gap; if resources are scarce, change the opening rather than assume the purchase works.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 326 (2023-11-22); costs and opening arithmetic reflect the hosts’ described game assumptions.
claims.uncertainty: The episode offers multiple possible ways to find the resource and does not promise any one will be available.

claims.statement: Take Leadership as a safe opening when you need to secure the two-system expansion, command tokens, and flexibility to follow Technology, Diplomacy or Warfare.
claims.conditions: It protects a baseline round more than it guarantees an exceptional one; its ceiling rises if other cards and trade timing line up.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 326 (2023-11-22); strategy-card timing assumptions not independently checked.
claims.uncertainty: The speakers agree on reliability but distinguish this from the higher upside of Trade or unusually favorable openings.

claims.statement: Prefer Trade when an early pick is available: it can fund Malice, the second carrier, technology and additional production in one round.
claims.conditions: The hosts describe the biggest upside when Ghosts pick first or second and receive favorable commodity exchanges; availability and table terms determine the actual return.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 326 (2023-11-22); card text and commodity arithmetic not independently checked.
claims.uncertainty: The very high round-one income described is a best-case estimate, not a baseline expectation.

claims.statement: Technology is a comfortable opening when timing matters: take Sling Relay, use it to build a dreadnought that can reach Malice, and keep the carrier available for another system.
claims.conditions: This line is presented as stable rather than spectacular; it is useful when Trade is unavailable and the action sequence fits.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 326 (2023-11-22); Sling Relay interaction and costs not independently checked.
claims.uncertainty: The hosts say this opening is comfortable, not the strongest possible outcome.

claims.statement: Take Warfare when a hostile or unreliable table makes expansion and production timing too risky; Ghosts can rebuild at home and still send the new plastic toward useful systems.
claims.conditions: This may mean delaying first-round technology, but the hosts consider early plastic more important than preserving theoretical card value when expansion would otherwise fail.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 326 (2023-11-22); secondary and timing rules not independently checked.
claims.uncertainty: The speakers call Warfare non-ideal but explicitly support it when needed.

claims.statement: Treat Diplomacy as timing-sensitive: take a valuable system before refreshing it when possible, and coordinate with Technology and Warfare players before selecting the card.
claims.conditions: If Malice is the only system available to refresh alongside home, Diplomacy can be poor; a different early planet may make the card worthwhile.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 326 (2023-11-22); card timing and refresh assumptions not independently checked.
claims.uncertainty: The hosts openly report that they often mis-sequence Diplomacy and disagree only in emphasis, not that it is always bad.

claims.statement: Use Politics selectively: selling speaker to the Trade holder can finance the opening, but may concede the first round-two pick and Custodians. Retaining speaker has value only if the round-two plan remains realistic.
claims.conditions: The hosts favor it when Trade and table timing can support the opening, not as the default fix for limited plastic or a narrow first expansion. Income requires an agreed speaker sale or another deal; Politics does not directly grant trade goods.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 326 (2023-11-22); round-one Custodians race depends on map and ruleset.
claims.uncertainty: This is a caution, not a universal ban; the guide also recognizes cases where Politics feeds Trade or an Imperial follow-up.

claims.statement: Choose Construction when a forward dock is genuinely needed and Diplomacy would mainly benefit other players; otherwise favor immediate plastic or another opening goal.
claims.conditions: The hosts like a forward system with negotiated wormhole access and a dock but warn that round-one Sling Relay plus a dock can overconcentrate resources in infrastructure.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 326 (2023-11-22); strategy-card and dock costs not independently checked.
claims.uncertainty: The hosts disagree in tone and call Construction situational rather than a preferred default.

claims.statement: Adopt a friendly, flexible IFF posture because other players’ use of your wormholes can create access and bargaining opportunities for Ghosts.
claims.conditions: Early and midgame openness can encourage trades and divert opponents toward each other; late game may call for a specific placement, and wormhole access also exposes Ghosts to attack.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 326 (2023-11-22); table politics and binding-deal rules not independently checked.
claims.uncertainty: The speakers describe a table-dependent political strategy, not guaranteed cooperation or income.

claims.statement: Use Creuss Iff when the recipient can place or move a wormhole to a planet they control or a non-home system without another player’s ship; it is most useful for seeding future Ghost routes before ships occupy the intended systems.
claims.conditions: The hosts emphasize that a player cannot use the note in a system containing another player’s ship unless the planet-control option applies; explain the restrictions before trading it.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 326 (2023-11-22); note wording should be checked against the current rules reference.
claims.uncertainty: The episode contains ASR misspellings of the faction note; the reference file identifies it as Creuss Iff.

claims.statement: Unlock Sai Seravus by establishing units in three alpha/beta wormhole systems, and use its ability to add fighters when capacity ships move through wormholes into the active system.
claims.conditions: The fighter appears per eligible ship, not per wormhole; the destination must be the active system and unused capacity must remain. The hosts describe Carrier II and adequate fleet supply as helpful for making the ability pay off.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 326 (2023-11-22); commander and timing details not independently rules-checked.
claims.uncertainty: The guide’s speech-recognized name is garbled, but the component reference identifies Sai Seravus; conditional ability details follow the speakers’ reading.

claims.statement: Place mechs to protect planets and preserve ground-force coverage; treat the Icarus Drive’s wormhole-token move as an occasional late-game option rather than its main job.
claims.conditions: Removing the mech sacrifices a ground unit and can weaken defense; the hosts estimate they use the effect only a small number of times and suggest it is less attractive when IFF or Wormhole Generator suffices.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 326 (2023-11-22); mech ability and timing not independently checked.
claims.uncertainty: The speakers frame the ability as useful but secondary, with frequency dependent on the board and deals.

claims.statement: Make Carrier II an early technology priority because capacity and movement support wormhole jumps and the commander’s fighter generation.
claims.conditions: The hosts usually place it after round-one Sling Relay, and regard its value as greatest when Ghosts can regularly move through wormholes; exact path depends on skips and available Technology picks.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 326 (2023-11-22); upgrade prerequisites and costs not independently checked.
claims.uncertainty: The hosts call Carrier II a need within their preferred plan, while acknowledging variation in how technology is acquired.

claims.statement: Keep the technology plan shallow: prioritize Sling Relay or Dark Energy Tap for the opening, Carrier II, then Light/Wave Deflector; additional blue tech is optional rather than a reason to delay ships.
claims.conditions: The hosts say DET is attractive when Ghosts can survive without opening Sling Relay, and Light/Wave’s value is strongest because Ghosts need to concentrate limited combat power where it matters.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 326 (2023-11-22); technology strategy and prerequisites not independently checked.
claims.uncertainty: They call several technologies wants and adapt to map skips, resources and objectives; this is a priority order, not a fixed sequence.

claims.statement: Consider Fighter II as a useful supplement: fighters generated during wormhole movement can remain behind as a defensive screen, reducing the need to build fighters directly.
claims.conditions: The ability requires eligible capacity movement and unused capacity; fighter upgrades are optional if Ghosts have more urgent plastic or tech needs.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 326 (2023-11-22); commander and unit-upgrade interactions not independently checked.
claims.uncertainty: The guide makes the trail-of-fighters image conditional on unlocking the commander and using the network often.

claims.statement: Treat Dimensional Splicer as a situational defensive bonus rather than a required red-tech detour; the speakers differ on how much its start-of-combat hit changes outcomes.
claims.conditions: Research it when a cheap red skip or free agenda-phase opportunity makes the cost small and wormhole systems need extra defense; prioritize ships and core movement first.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 326 (2023-11-22); tech wording and hit timing not independently checked.
claims.uncertainty: The speakers explicitly contest its value: one values assigned hits and deterrence, the other doubts a single start-of-combat hit swings enough fights.

claims.statement: Research Wormhole Generator when table cooperation is drying up or Ghosts need independent late-game wormhole placement; it can also create a stall and set up the hero.
claims.conditions: The hosts call it optional, often a round-four or round-five purchase if extra resources remain; weigh its cost against a mech’s cheaper one-off relocation and the opening technology priorities.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 326 (2023-11-22); Omega tech details not independently checked.
claims.uncertainty: The hosts agree it is useful insurance but debate whether repeated use justifies its price in a friendly game.

claims.statement: Save Riftwalker Meian for a high-impact system swap: the hero can create access for control objectives, move units into reach, or expose a target to attack.
claims.conditions: The hero unlocks after three scored objectives; the swapped systems must contain wormholes or units and cannot be the Creuss home system or Wormhole Nexus. Plan around the actual board and objective requirements.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 326 (2023-11-22); hero wording and objective interactions not independently rules-checked.
claims.uncertainty: The speakers give examples and call out boundaries, but each proposed play still depends on exact objective and map state.

claims.statement: Use the hero’s late-game reliability to prepare difficult control objectives instead of spreading forces thin to qualify for every possible objective early.
claims.conditions: The guide cites Rule Distant Lands and Achieved Supremacy as examples; partial setup is not scoring, and the necessary final control and objective conditions must still be met.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 326 (2023-11-22); objective wording and hero eligibility not independently checked.
claims.uncertainty: The speakers call the swap a strong option, not a guarantee; opponents may disrupt the position or the exact requirement may differ.

claims.statement: Stay friendly while sharing routes, but avoid making your own territory an easy target: seed a compact, mutually reinforcing wormhole network and defend valuable systems.
claims.conditions: The hosts recommend choosing one objective to secure rather than thinly contesting every point of the board; expect that some attacks are the cost of offering wormhole access.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 326 (2023-11-22); opponent incentives vary by table.
claims.uncertainty: The defensive posture is strategic advice, not a promise that deterrence prevents attacks.

claims.statement: Value Malice as an early economic foothold, but plan for retreat or eventual loss rather than over-defending it at the expense of stronger wormhole-linked bases.
claims.conditions: The hosts expect its early trade goods and access to help, while later preferring high-value systems that reinforce Ghosts’ economy and defensive network.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 326 (2023-11-22); planet yields and token effects not independently checked.
claims.uncertainty: Whether to keep Malice depends on opponents, retreat routes, and the relative value of other controlled planets.

claims.statement: Treat wormhole-related agendas as major survival risks: the hosts favor opposing or burying Wormhole Research and Wormhole Reconstruction because their against outcomes can destroy ships or lock systems with command tokens.
claims.conditions: The risk is greatest when valuable fleets or home positions depend on alpha/beta wormholes; the guide acknowledges that another player’s assets in wormhole systems can make opposition easier.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 326 (2023-11-22); agenda names and outcomes not independently verified.
claims.uncertainty: This advice reflects the hosts’ reading of the printed outcomes; edition, agenda deck and table context can change the decision.

claims.statement: Enforced Travel Ban can favor Ghosts if passed because Quantum Entanglement still preserves Ghosts’ alpha/beta adjacency while other players lose movement through those wormholes.
claims.conditions: Its against outcome can destroy PDS, so consider objectives and structures before prioritizing it; the hosts generally advise a Politics player to bury the three dangerous wormhole agendas.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 326 (2023-11-22); rules interpretation is source-era opinion, not current-rules verification.
claims.uncertainty: The guide’s assessment depends on the stated interaction between the law and faction ability; current official interpretation was not checked.

claims.statement: Nexus Sovereignty is favorable in either outcome as the hosts describe it: it limits movement through Wormhole Nexus alpha/beta holes or places a gamma wormhole at Mecatol Rex, creating a route for the agent.
claims.conditions: This is especially welcome if Ghosts hold Malice; a gamma link to Mecatol can make Fleet Logistics more attractive for a hero-and-action finish.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 326 (2023-11-22); agenda and ability interaction not independently checked.
claims.uncertainty: The positive evaluation is tied to the particular outcomes read aloud in the episode.

claims.statement: Do not assume Ghosts will win the Custodians race; the hosts see early access as possible but less reliable than using movement, Imperial timing, or a strong late-game objective push.
claims.conditions: Starting influence and table timing still matter despite Malice and wormhole mobility; this is a long-run tendency, not a prediction for every map or game.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 326 (2023-11-22); Custodians timing and current rules not independently reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: The hosts explicitly note Ghosts can take Mecatol early or pursue it later, but describe early access as a relative weakness.

connections.conditions: At the start of round one, the hosts use the agent to make home and Malice adjacent for a tactical action, enabling the commonly described Malice opening.
Carrier II capacity and movement help eligible ships move through wormholes and retain unused capacity for the commander’s fighter placement.
Moving a Creuss wormhole token to a useful origin can provide a system from which Ghost ships gain Slipstream movement; this is one optional late-game use discussed by the hosts.
The speakers describe Fleet Logistics as useful for acting immediately after the hero’s system swap, allowing a follow-up action before opponents respond.
Placing alpha/beta wormholes with a cooperative partner can help reach the commander’s three-system unlock condition; the guide proposes a reciprocal Alliance arrangement.
A buyer may distrust the IFF if Ghosts retain mechs that can later remove wormhole tokens; the hosts recommend building trust and treating mech relocation as occasional.
